title: Good Node Count
statement:
Count the tree nodes whose value is not beaten by any ancestor.

Contract
- `root` may be null. Each node has an integer `value` and nullable `left` and `right` children.
- A node is good when no node on the path from the root down to it (excluding itself) has a strictly greater value. The root is always good, and a value equal to the largest ancestor still counts.
- Return how many nodes are good; an empty tree has none. Values may be negative or repeated.
- Do not modify the tree. Trees may be lopsided, with a height of up to 1000 nodes.

Examples
- `[6, 2, 7, 6, null, 3, 9]` has 4 good nodes: `6`, `7`, the left-hand `6` (it ties the root) and `9`.
- A null tree has 0 good nodes.
- `[9, 5, null, 4]` shrinks downward, so only the root is good.
hints: Whether a node is good depends only on the path above it, not on its siblings or descendants.
Carry the largest value seen so far down the recursion and compare each node against it before updating it for the children.

Visit every node once. Intended complexity: O(n) time for n nodes. Space is the recursion depth: O(h) for tree height h, which is O(log n) for a balanced tree (the workload uses balanced trees) and O(n) for a chain.
inputSyntax: Input: the tree in level order with null for missing children, for example: [6, 2, 7, 6, null, 3, 9]
